findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/closeout-trust.ts:606-675 — The promised separation between review retention and artifact authority is not mechanically enforced. classifyCurrentCloseoutArtifactForReviewRetention accepts a same-UID-forgeable causal receipt and keeps the signed review current, while validateCurrentCloseoutArtifact always returns invalid because latestValidCloseoutReceipt is deliberately null. rg shows validateCurrentCloseoutArtifact has no production gate consumer (only closeout-trust-smoke); production artifact readers consume test/summary/delivery/live-smoke evidence through their separate readers without canonical writer provenance. Therefore a local actor can replace an artifact and co-commit a forged causal receipt, preserve the review, and reach the ordinary artifact consumer without the re-review that previously supplied the only writer-authority boundary. Either add an actual independently authoritative admissibility check to every registered artifact consumer (isolated signature/capability or equivalent), or keep such post-review writes review-invalidating; comments/tests that an unused helper remains fail-closed are insufficient.

packages/main/src/handlers/done-prepare.ts:1442-1468 — The new convergence counters do not measure the closeout history they claim to prove. metadataRollbacks and humanConfirmations only regex the current invocation step text; reviewerReattestations counts current blocking runbook rows (which is necessarily zero on PASS), not new reviewer runs/passes; successfulCloseout is only the final snapshot. A story that already rolled back, received a human story_resume, or re-attested reviewers before this invocation still renders all zero. The smoke test constructs the same final snapshot, so it cannot catch this. Capture a closeout baseline and derive counts from persisted signed process events/review-run/pass identities and validation receipts over that interval, including initial/final phase/round/receipt identity, then assert those measured counts before PASS.

packages/main/src/handlers/validate-concept.ts:120-155 — scanDeletedSymbols is still a line regex keyed only by declaration kind+name, not the declaration/file/scope/signature identity required by CHK-003. It ignores class methods/constructors and collapses overloads/same-name declarations. Repro against current dist: a diff replacing `export function f(x: string): string;` with `export function f(x: number): number;` returns [], and a changed method signature also returns []; thus removal of one overload/signature can be hidden by any added same-name declaration. The focused smoke passes because it tests only an unmatched removed overload and explicitly narrows methods/constructors out of scope, contradicting the must verification intents. Implement declaration-aware identity (or an explicit fail-closed parser/ambiguity diagnostic) and cover same-name overload/scope/signature replacement, methods, and constructors.

CHK-003 must coverage is materially incomplete and the recorded evidence overclaims it. scanDeletedSymbols is still regex-based and collapses declarations to kind:name, so deleting one overload while another same-name overload remains is hidden; it also ignores non-exported TypeScript functions, class methods, and constructors even though CHK-003:edge:2 explicitly requires those supported forms and deterministic same-name/scope handling. The smoke test instead asserts those forms are outside the deletion surface, and its overload case removes the only same-name declaration, so it cannot prove CHK-003:adversarial:2. Replace name-only pairing with declaration identity/multiplicity (scope/kind/signature or an explicit bounded supported surface), then add a retained-same-name overload negative and the required non-exported/method/constructor cases before claiming all must intents covered.

CHK-002 one-pass acceptance counters are not measured from lifecycle history, so DONE prepare can report zero-cost convergence without proving it. deriveDonePreparePassConvergence infers metadataRollbacks/humanConfirmations by regexing only current step text and reviewerReattestations from current blocking runbook rows; it does not bind initial/final phase, review round/receipt identity, actual artifact writer sequence, or prior re-attestation/ack/backstep events. closeoutWriteSequence is a constant string. The positive smoke mostly asserts the resulting literal zeros, so a past metadata-only rollback or reviewer re-attestation is invisible. Emit counters from durable process events/review receipt identity and artifact receipts over the closeout window, and add a negative fixture containing a prior backstep/re-attestation/human ack that must make PASS convergence fail.

packages/main/src/handlers/validate-concept.ts:120-155 — HIGH: scanDeletedSymbols keys removed/added declarations only by kind+name across the entire multi-file diff. A retained declaration edit in one file therefore cancels a true deletion of the same-named export in another file, causing the concept preflight to miss the deletion and potentially skip lattice-review-concept. Repro after build: feed a diff that deletes export function shared from src/a.ts while changing export function shared in src/b.ts; scanDeletedSymbols returns [] instead of [shared]. Track current diff file (and Python declaration scope where applicable) in the declaration identity, while keeping same-file signature/body edits paired; add the cross-file duplicate-name regression.

packages/main/src/handlers/done-prepare.ts:1442-1467 — MEDIUM: the advertised convergence counters are inferred from absence/presence of phrases in the final DonePrepareStep text, not from durable lifecycle events. metadataRollbacks and humanConfirmations default to zero whenever those words are absent; reviewerReattestations counts only current blocking rows (a completed re-attestation is zero); unchangedSuiteExecutions is forced to zero whenever the output is not recognized as reused. Thus a run can print successfulCloseout=1 and all-zero counters after earlier metadata rollback/re-attestation/human intervention, so the acceptance metric is cosmetic rather than the requested mechanical proof. Derive counts from bounded process-event/receipt deltas for this closeout attempt (or rename them to current-run diagnostics and add a real one-pass integration assertion over event history).

F-005 is only partially fixed: collectDonePrepareConvergenceFacts counts reviewer runs/passes strictly after the successful TEST entry (`startedAt > testEntry.timestamp` / `createdAt > testEntry.timestamp`). The costly failure this story targets can re-run review while the story is still in REVIEW—e.g. transition-time validation writes metadata, REVIEW→TEST remains blocked, and reviewers re-attest before the eventual successful TEST transition. Those extra identities occur between the REVIEW anchor and TEST entry, so current telemetry reports reviewerReattestations=0 and DONE prepare may claim zero-cost convergence. The existing negative test injects reviewerIdentityIds directly and never exercises this collector window. Bind the initial complete-review receipt identities at the REVIEW anchor (or otherwise establish a baseline), count additional valid run/pass identities from that baseline through closeout including the pre-TEST interval, and add a real-store fixture with an extra pre-TEST reviewer run/pass that makes the PASS convergence invariant fail.
